base.motivation: Given your low heat tolerance (3/10) and the steep initial climb starting at km 1.1 (19.6% gradient), you will generate significant metabolic heat. A highly breathable, fast-drying synthetic short-sleeve shirt is selected as your active base layer to maximize moisture management. A long-sleeve synthetic shirt is packed as a dry spare for the descent.

items.name: Men's Hiking Synthetic SS T-Shirt MH500

middle.motivation: At departure, the apparent temperature is cool (7.8°C). A lightweight, highly breathable micro-fleece is recommended to be worn initially to prevent cold-start shivering, but should be shed quickly once the steep climb begins. A warmer, grid-structured fleece is packed for the cooler descent and summit areas.

insulation.motivation: The apparent temperature drops to a chilly 3.9°C around km 4 (the high point of the route). A packable down puffer jacket is essential in your backpack to provide thermal protection during rest stops or in case of emergency.

shell.motivation: There is a 30% probability of precipitation around km 2, and wind exposure is likely on the mountain sections. A highly breathable, fully waterproof 3-layer hard shell is packed to shield you from wind chill and potential dampness without causing overheating.

pants.motivation: Long pants are recommended to protect your legs from brush, rocks, and the cool mountain air (7-10°C) across the technical terrain.

shoes.motivation: With 67% of the route classified as mountain hiking and steep gradients, high-cut hiking shoes are required to provide necessary ankle support and traction on technical surfaces.

gear.motivation: Trekking poles are highly recommended to reduce joint impact and improve stability on the steep 17-19% gradients and technical mountain paths.

overall_strategy: Your low heat tolerance means you must avoid overheating and sweating heavily during the two major climbs (gradients up to 19.6%). Start the hike with a lightweight fleece over your synthetic short-sleeve base layer, but strip down to the base layer as soon as the climb begins. Keep your high-performance hard shell and down jacket in your pack, ready to deploy at the summit or during breaks where the apparent temperature drops to 3.9°C.
